newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African steel product stocks dip in December.
newsitem.headline: S.African steel product stocks dip in December.

text.p: Stocks of South African steel products dropped 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted 2.41 million tons in December from November's 2.53 million tons, the Central Statistical Service said on Wednesday.
The trend has been downwards since April, 1996, and the drop represents a 12.6 percent fall on levels in December, 1995.
The monthly drop is mostly due to a fall in ferro-alloys to 167,574 tons, from 239,892 tons in November -- an all-time low for the survey.
Ingots and other primary forms dipped by 15,908 tons to 311,746.
However, some areas rose with flat-rolled products hitting 1.07 million tons from 0.96 million tons in November -- but still well short of the 1.14 million tons seen in December, 1995.

Prices in the steel market -- both internationally and locally -- have been bumping along the bottom of the economic cycle. Both South African steel giants, Iscor and Highveld Steel, have issued profit warnings in recent months.
Analysts see drops in stock levels as an encouraging sign that could herald a tightening of supply to the market and so trigger off rising prices again.
